problem: It says dropping the factor 60 gives 0.083 L/min. Dropping 60 actually gives a value in L/s, so the number is 0.083 L/s, which equals 5 L/min. The unit L/min is wrong and would mislead a student.
fix: With I = 5 mg and A = 60 mg·s/L, dropping 60 gives 0.083 L/s (not L/min), which is the same as 5 L/min.

problem: It says 'The area between the first-pass curve and this extrapolated line is A.' That describes the recirculation area, not the first-pass area. A is the area under the first-pass curve: the measured part up to recirculation plus the area under the extrapolated line after that.
fix: The area under the first-pass curve — the measured part plus the extrapolated part — is A. Equivalently, take the area under the original curve up to the start of recirculation, then add the area under the extrapolated line from that time onward.
